'''Wendell Talbot Hill III''' (born 1952) is an American physicist and professor at the [[University of Maryland, College Park|University of Maryland]]. His research career has largely focused on the intersection of laser physics and [[Quantum|quantum science]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Celebrating Black in Physical Sciences Colloquium lecture series launches {{!}} UCI |url=https://ps.uci.edu/news/2816 |access-date=2023-03-17 |website=ps.uci.edu |language=en}}</ref>
== Early life and education ==
Wendell Hill was born in 1952 in [[Berkeley, California]]. His father, Wendell Hill, Jr., was the Chief Pharmacist at in the [[University of California, Irvine Medical Center|Orange County Medical Center]] (now the [[University of California, Irvine Medical Center|University of California Irvine Medical Center]]) in the 1960s, and later served as dean of Howard University’s College of Pharmacy in the 1990s. His mother, Marcella Washington Hill, was a mathematics teacher who taught at the [[University of the District of Columbia]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Wendell Hill's Biography |url=https://www.thehistorymakers.org/biography/wendell-hill |access-date=2023-03-17 |website=The HistoryMakers |language=en}}</ref>

Hill attended and graduated from [[Villa Park High School]] in [[Orange, California]], in 1970. For his undergraduate studies, he attended the [[University of California, Irvine]], where he received his bachelor's degree in physics in 1974. In 1976, he received his master's degree in physics from [[Stanford University]], and in 1980, he earned a PhD in physics from [[Stanford University]].<ref name=":3">Hill, Wendell T. Resume of Wendell T. Hill. Box 1, folder 21. Ronald E. Mickens collection on African-American physicists, circa 1950-2008. Niels Bohr Library & Archives, American Institute of Physics. 3 April 2023. https://libserv.aip.org/ipac20/ipac.jsp?session=1C80N465R3370.1846&menu=search&aspect=power&npp=10&ipp=20&spp=20&profile=rev-all&ri=1&source=%7E%21horizon&index=.GW&term=Hill%2C+Wendell+T.&x=0&y=0&aspect=power</ref> At Stanford, he was an IBM pre-doctoral fellow (1974-1975)<ref name=":3" /> and his thesis was titled "Intracavity Absorption Spectroscopy" and submitted in July 1980.<ref name=":4">{{cite thesis |id={{ProQuest|303065514}} |last1=Hill |first1=Wendell Talbot |date=1980 |title=Intracavity Absorption Spectroscopy }}</ref> His thesis advisor was [[Arthur Leonard Schawlow|Arthur L. Schawlow]], and [[Theodor W. Hänsch]] and [[Richard Zare]] were also on his thesis advisory committee. Hill was also a member of the Schawlow/Hänsch research group while at Stanford.<ref name=":4" />

== Career ==
From 1980 to 1982, Hill was a [[National Research Council (United States)|National Research Council]] postdoctoral fellow at the [[National Institute of Standards and Technology|National Bureau of Standards]] (now the [[National Institute of Standards and Technology|National Institute of Standards & Technology]]), in [[Gaithersburg, Maryland]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Atoms, Molecules and Light - Physics Serving Society - Wendell T. Hill, III |url=https://pswscience.org/meeting/atoms-molecules-and-light/ |access-date=2023-03-17 |website=PSW Science |language=en}}</ref> He subsequently joined the faculty at the Institute for Physical Science and Technology (IPST) at the [[University of Maryland, College Park|University of Maryland]]. He began as a research assistant scientist, before being promoted to assistant professor and later associate professor.<ref name=":3" /> In 1996, Hill was made full professor at the [[University of Maryland, College Park|University of Maryland]], and in 2006 he became a fellow of the Joint Quantum Institute.<ref name=":0" />

During his career, his has held visiting teaching and research positions at the [[Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory|Lawrence Livermore National Labsoratory]],<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Professor Wendell Hill '74 Colloquium - Precision Measurement of the Quantum Vacuum with Petawatt Lasers {{!}} UCI |url=https://ps.uci.edu/events/2762 |access-date=2023-03-17 |website=ps.uci.edu}}</ref> the [[Venezuelan Institute for Scientific Research|Instituto Venezalano de Investigaciones]], the [[Paris-Sud University|Université de Paris, Orsay]], as Guest Scientist at the [[National Institute of Standards and Technology|NIST]], and at [[JILA]] at the [[University of Colorado Boulder|University of Colorado, Boulder]].<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":3" />

Between 1999 and 2002, Hill was director of the Laboratory for Atomic, Molecular & Optical Science, and Engineering at the [[University of Maryland, College Park|University of Maryland]]. From 2010 to 2012 he was Program Director of the Atomic, Molecular and Optical (AMO) Physics program at the [[NSF International|NSF]].<ref name=":0" />

Hill has held multiple professional appointments throughout his career. He has served as an executive committee member of the Division of Laser Science and the Committee on Minorities for the [[American Physical Society]], and chaired the Optical Physics Technical Group for [[Optica (society)|Optical Society of America]] (now [[Optica (society)|Optica]]). He also chaired the Committee on Atomic Molecular and Optical Science and the Board on Physics and Astronomy for the [[National Academy of Sciences]].<ref>Mickens, Ronald (1999). The African American Presence in Physics. Atlanta, Georgia: National Society of Black Physicists. p. 63. https://radar.auctr.edu/islandora/object/cau.ir%3A1999_mickens_ronald_e</ref>

As of 2022, he is also director of the graduate Chemical Physics Program at the University of Maryland.<ref name=":2" />

== Research ==
Hill's research has focused on ultrafast dynamics and quantum information, as well as on topics such as high-energy particle physics to ultracold atoms.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2" />

== Awards ==

* Presidential Young Investigator Award (now the Presidential Early Career Award), [[National Science Foundation]] (NSF), 1985<ref name=":0" />
* Fellow, the [[American Physical Society]] (APS)<ref name=":2" />
* Fellow, the [[National Society of Black Physicists]] (NSBP)<ref name=":2" />
* Fellow, the African Scientific Institute<ref name=":2" />
* Member, the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]], 2023 <ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.amacad.org/new-members-2023 | title=New Members }}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Hill married his wife, Patricia Hill, while at [[Stanford University]], and they have three children.<ref name=":4" /><ref name=":0" />
